name: Project Constants
blurb: board size, supply voltages and mechanical references kept in one place
intro: One list of the numbers every room uses - board outline, rails, holes, heights, temperatures - saved as the project's record in the app. It checks names, units and tolerances, works out the min/max limits, and writes the same list as a C header, Python, OpenSCAD and JSON.

inputs.label: Constants
inputs.help: Value: a number (3.3, 4k7), a range (-20..60) or text (ENIG). Tolerance: ±0.2, ±5% or +0.1/-0.05.

usage: Pass `constants` as rows {name, value, unit, tol, group, note}: value is a number in engineering notation, a range 'min..max' or text; tol is '±0.2', '±5%' or '+0.1/-0.05'; group is board, power, mechanical, thermal, interface, environment or other. It returns the rows per group with min/max limits, warnings for bad names, duplicates, missing units and unreadable tolerances, and the list as C header, Python, OpenSCAD and JSON texts. The project's saved list is read or written with the MCP tool tool_data (id project-constants, data {constants: [...]}); read it before using a board size or rail voltage.
sources: ISO 80000-1:2022 (a value is a number times a unit; units written after the number)
ISO 273 clearance holes for bolts and screws (the M3 example)
